risks: ⚠️ SURVIVAL: the Sept 1, 2026 6-K showed the going-concern working-capital deficit at $205.2M (more than double the $87.1M in the Mar 2026 20-F). Another equity raise remains likely despite the company's $300M buyback authorization.
Guidance credibility: Q2 revenue of $65.4M vs the $127M consensus makes the $360M FY26 guide look stretched. Another miss would likely break the 52-week low decisively.
Legal overhang: a Pomerantz investigation on behalf of investors was announced Oct 23, 2026.
Heavy losses (TTM net loss ~$183M) and an acquisition-heavy revenue base make organic growth hard to read.
Leadership changes announced Oct 22 add execution uncertainty during a critical cost-cut period.

macroRisk.inflationNote: Sep PCE: headline 3.6% y/y (+0.5% m/m), core 3.1% y/y (+0.3% m/m); Q3 GDP +3.4% annualized. Oct CPI on Nov 10 is the next test — core ≥0.4% m/m would effectively lock in the December hike.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Going-concern working-capital deficit plus heavy losses. Rates and risk appetite set both the multiple and the terms of any refinancing.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — a going-concern AI small cap is highly exposed to a December hike and the AI/data-center regulatory overhang from the Nov 3 midterms.

postWin.note: The isolated day-of reaction to the Sept 1, 2026 H1 print was not cleanly separable in this research pass, but the stock is down a cumulative ~17.5% from $2.57 (Aug 3) to $2.12 (Sept 29) across the period spanning both the H1 print and the Sept 23 cost-cut announcement — net negative, materially worse than the prior report's muted-but-flat +3.1% framing. Roth Capital cutting its target to $6.50 from $9.50 on the print is direct evidence the going-concern deficit escalation is now outweighing the revenue beat in the market's read. NOTE: catalystType earnings_beat has only n=2 in the turbo skill-feedback dataset — Tier 1, context only, no tier2 directive applies.

postLose.note: BigBear.ai (BBAI), a similarly ATM/dilution-dependent AI micro-cap, fell 11.3% the day after missing Q1 2025 estimates. The more relevant tail case is now Canoo (GOEV): disclosed the same going-concern language RZLV's deficit now mirrors at a larger scale, was never able to resolve it, and was delisted after a Chapter 7 filing — the real downside case now that RZLV's own deficit has more than doubled in one filing period.

comparableCases.event: Sept 1 H1 2026 print (revenue ~20x YoY, guidance reaffirmed) + Sept 23 cost-cut announcement — going-concern deficit more than doubles to $205.2M
comparableCases.note: Own-company precedent showing the market now discounts even a very strong revenue beat once the going-concern deficit escalates — net price action was negative across both the H1 print and the follow-up mitigation announcement, the clearest evidence yet that survival risk now dominates the growth narrative.

comparableCases.event: Q1 2025 EPS/revenue miss — dilution-risk AI micro-cap punished on a bad print
comparableCases.note: BigBear.ai, a similarly dilution/ATM-dependent AI micro-cap, fell 11.3% the day after missing Q1 2025 estimates — a real base rate for how a weak update could hit RZLV given its own going-concern overhang.

comparableCases.event: ATM-funded balance-sheet turnaround — 90%+ debt reduction, $693M raised via equity facilities, ended FY2025 with $462M cash
comparableCases.note: Shows an ATM/dilution-dependent AI micro-cap can use the same mechanism RZLV is now relying on to genuinely fix its balance sheet rather than just delay failure — the bull-case survival path for RZLV's own mitigation plan.

comparableCases.event: Going-concern doubt disclosed but never resolved — Chapter 7 bankruptcy filing and Nasdaq delisting
comparableCases.note: Canoo disclosed the same kind of going-concern language RZLV's filings now carry at a larger and worsening scale, was unable to secure sufficient additional funding, and ultimately filed Chapter 7 and was delisted — the real tail-risk case now that RZLV's own working-capital deficit has more than doubled in a single filing period.
